title: Newcastle and Moore, Oklahoma · May 20, 2013
summary: One tornado across two county records, with a source-backed account of its path, warnings, school and hospital impacts, and the limits of reported clocks and later damage revisions.

records.basis: McClain County segment names the Newcastle-Moore tornado and explicitly continues into Cleveland County FIPS 027. Its ending at20:04UTC and [-97.605,35.303] matches the Cleveland segment beginning. Same episode 74673 and the original NWS whole-track account corroborate the association. Reviewed October 19, 2026 UTC without merging or rewriting source fields.

Cleveland County narrative explicitly continues the Newcastle-Moore tornado from McClain across the Canadian River near I-44. Its beginning matches the McClain ending in reported time and coordinates. The shared episode is supporting context, not the sole identity rule. Reviewed October 19, 2026 UTC against retained source fields and the NWS whole-track account.

observations.title: Plaza Towers teachers reported a change of shelter within the original building
observations.locator: NIST SP1164 section 4.2, printed page 29 / PDF page 53, interview account and footnotes 35 to 37.
observations.account: NIST reports teacher interviews describing one group moving from a hallway in the original main classroom building into nearby bathrooms and a closet as skylights began lifting. The account describes less fallen debris in those rooms than in adjoining hallways.
observations.limits: Later interview testimony about particular occupants and spaces, not continuous observation of every person or a synchronized shelter timeline. This does not establish a tested room capacity, certify a shelter or isolate the cause of survival.

observations.review: Selected original NIST PDF text re-read October 19, 2026 UTC. Printed-page and PDF-page locators checked against the original text. Teacher testimony, surveyed outcomes and proposed explanations remain source-attributed. observations.title: Roof and wall damage differed within the original Plaza Towers building
observations.locator: NIST SP1164 section 4.2, printed page 31 / PDF page 55, original main classroom building account and footnote 40.
observations.account: NIST documents roof-system loss and perimeter-wall collapse in the southwest wing of the original building. Other portions sustained partial roof loss without collapsing. NIST suggests steel-frame redundancy and support not solely dependent on roof bracing as a likely explanation. A teacher interview reports roof loss before wall collapse.
observations.limits: Observed damage, teacher testimony and NIST interpretation are distinct evidence. The suggested explanation is not an independently isolated causal result. No local wind, complete failure sequence, exact collapse time, component load or resistance is measured by this observation.

observations.title: Briarwood Building 400 combined a reported refuge change with different damage
observations.locator: NIST SP1164 section 4.3, printed page 36 / PDF page 60, teacher interviews and footnotes 43 to 48; printed page 38 / PDF page 62, Building 400 performance account. Compare the older rating statement on printed page 34 / PDF page 58 with the separate retained NCEI revision.
observations.account: NIST reports teachers moving Building 400 occupants from its main hallway into bathrooms as the tornado approached. Its survey describes this building as less structurally damaged than other Briarwood buildings, with perimeter walls essentially intact despite some roof loss. Roof and window damage nevertheless caused significant interior damage.
observations.limits: Reported actions and surveyed aftermath are not a calibrated causal comparison or a guarantee about bathrooms. The full Briarwood survey photograph hosted by Atlas is not registered to Building 400 or its shelter spaces. NIST retains an initial EF5 site interpretation; the separate retained NCEI narrative later supports EF4 at Briarwood, while the whole-track maximum remains EF5.
